content.title: About
content.content: Ravioli are small pasta parcels filled with a mixture of cheese and spinach. This version is served without sauce, allowing the delicate dough and aromatic filling to shine.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Traditional ravioli originate from Italy and have been made for over a thousand years.
The cheese‑and‑spinach combination provides a good balance of protein and vitamins.
Without sauce, ravioli are often finished with olive oil, fresh herbs, or grated Parmesan.
Spinach retains most of its nutrients thanks to the short cooking time.
A sauce‑free version is convenient for those watching calories and sugar intake.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Cheese and spinach together supply a complete set of amino acids that support tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Calcium source
items.content: Cheese provides a substantial amount of calcium, essential for bone and teeth health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Spinach contains vitamin B6 and folate, which aid metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Leafy spinach is rich in lutein and vitamin C, helping protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Low sugar
items.content: The absence of sauce makes the dish lower in calories and with a low glycemic impact.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Cheese may cause discomfort for people who cannot digest lactose.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to milk proteins.

items.title: Oxalates in spinach
items.content: Spinach contains oxalates, which in excess can contribute to kidney stone formation.

items.title: Added sodium
items.content: Prepared ravioli sometimes contain added salt for flavor; those monitoring sodium should check the label.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Boil the ravioli in salted water for 3–4 minutes until al dente. Toss with a drizzle of olive oil, sprinkle with grated Parmesan and fresh herbs. They can also be added to salads or used as a base for a baked casserole.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep dry ravioli in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. Cooked ravioli store in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. Discard if any off‑odor or discoloration appears.
